dsh-opencode-patch

OpenCode on DeepSeek Harness
Gateway origin headers · Session affinity · Free-tier tool fallback · Live dual-mode quota meter

Quick Start · What this fixes · Interface · Configuration · Troubleshooting · Changelog · Contributing

--- `dsh-opencode-patch` is a DeepSeek Harness host plugin that keeps **OpenCode Zen & Go** models working inside DSH. Connect `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `gpt-5.4`, `gemini-3.8-flash`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free`, `qwen3.8-flash` and the rest of the OpenCode catalog without network rejections, Cloudflare challenges, entitlement mismatches, or invisible limits. **The default state.** Point DSH at OpenCode with no plugin and the models do not work at all — not on one shape, on any of them: - **The request is not recognised as coming from a coding agent.** DSH sends its own `User-Agent`, and no `x-opencode-client`, `x-opencode-project` or `x-opencode-session` at all, so the gateway sees an anonymous SDK call and the traffic falls under the abuse rules the vendor documents for clients that do not identify themselves. **The free tier is a separate matter and this is not its cause**: with every one of those headers restored, a CLI `User-Agent`, a valid session id and the `read`/`bash` tool schemas the fallback injects, a Zen `-free` model still answers `403 FreeTierError` from outside OpenCode while a paid model on the same request answers `200`. The ids are still offered — the refusal names itself, and hiding a row the vendor may serve is the worse failure — and the headers it restores are for the paid routes and the vendor's stated client rules. - **A turn without a session id is rejected or left unlinked.** Every turn has to carry a stable `ses_…`-shaped id, and DSH omits `sessionId` entirely for subagents, background evaluations and modes like **Auto Review**. - **Free-tier `/responses` bodies are refused without `read` and `bash` in `tools`**, and DSH deliberately does not send them. - **The catalog is thin.** A bare `/models` listing carries ids and little else, so the picker shows unnamed rows with no prices and no context windows. **What is left once those work is a different problem, and it is not about the account.** OpenCode serves its models on **four different API shapes**, while DSH picks a transport from the provider row — one route can speak one shape. So a model served on Responses, Messages or Mistral answers `500` the moment the basics are restored, which is why this plugin routes per **model** rather than per provider. **What this does.** It restores every missing protocol element at the network layer — **strictly for OpenCode routes** (`opencode` / `opencode-go` / `opencode-responses` / `opencode-anthropic` / `opencode-google`). All other traffic (DeepSeek, OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub) passes through untouched. **What you get.** A picker listing the whole OpenCode catalog with real names, prices and context windows; every model sent to the endpoint it is actually served on; and a live meter for the quota or the spend — no configuration. **Three things it is built around.** 1. **Minimal intrusion.** Nothing is patched globally: requests are intercepted only for the routes this plugin claims, and every other provider — DeepSeek, OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub — passes through byte-identical. The composer meter is one switch away from being gone, not one screen away from being tolerated. 2. **A native DSH plugin.** One `apply()`, a settings card bound to its own namespace, services declared through `ctx.inject`, slots filled the way the host fills its own, and copy in both bundled languages. No private hooks, no patched host code. 3. **OpenCode API compatibility.** The traits the gateways actually check are restored at the network layer — a `ses_…` id shaped exactly like the CLI's own, official origin headers, parent-session lineage, and the free-tier `read`/`bash` schema fallback. **Highlights** - 🔑 Deterministic `ses_<12hex><14base62>` session hashing with KV-cache affinity across turns, subagents and forks - 🌐 Gateway origin restoration — `User-Agent`, `x-opencode-client`, `x-opencode-project`, parent-session lineage - 🧰 Free-tier `read` + `bash` tool-schema fallback, so a free-tier body carries the tool definitions its endpoint requires — one cause of a `403` removed, and not the whole of it: the gateway's gate is not in the request, measured - 📇 OpenCode-catalog-backed (`models.opencode.ai`, the registry models.dev publishes) with offline shims and background SWR refresh — names, context windows, prices - ⭕ Live dual-mode composer meter — Go quota ring (5-hour / weekly / monthly) or Zen pay-as-you-go pill, plus session spend and model rate - 🕵️ Strict credential isolation — Zen keys (`oc_sk_…`) never query the Go quota endpoint **Contents** 1. [Deep Dive](./docs/deep-dive.md) — the protocol internals, out of this README 9. [Attribution & License](#-attribution--license) --- ## 🚀 Quick Start **1. Install** into your DSH Web profile (Node 24+): ```sh cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web npm install dsh-opencode-patch ``` The package is `dsh-opencode-patch` under every name it is used by: the dependency you install, the bundle entry in your profile, and the row the host resolves. It is also published as [`@viztor/dsh-opencode-patch`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@viztor/dsh-opencode-patch), and the older name [`@viztor/dsh-opencode`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@viztor/dsh-opencode) keeps publishing as a deprecated thin wrapper that re-exports it — an install still on that name keeps working, and moving to either of the other two is a rename rather than a fix. **2. Enable the bundle** — add the package to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` array: ```jsonc // ~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json { "dependencies": { "dsh-opencode-patch": "^1.8.0", }, "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["dsh-opencode-patch"], "patchReload": "live", }, }, } ``` **3. Add a credential** so the quota meter can resolve a key — store `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` (Go subscription, `sk-…`) and/or `OPENCODE_API_KEY` (Zen pay-as-you-go, `oc_sk_…`) in DSH Credentials or your environment. **4. Restart `dsh web`.** The host bundle is only imported at boot (`hmr root: []`), so a restart is what loads `lib/index.mjs`; client UI changes (`lib/client.js`) only need a browser refresh. Done — the **OpenCode Patch** card appears under _Settings → Plugins_, and the meter mounts in the composer dock as soon as an OpenCode model is active. --- ## 🔌 What This Fixes | Without the patch | With `dsh-opencode-patch` | | :-- | :-- | | Zen free models fail with `403 FreeTierError` | **Offered, and refused in the gateway's own words.** The headers and tool fallbacks are restored for the paid routes, but they are not this error's cause — measured with all of them in place, a Zen `-free` id still answers `403` while a paid model answers `200`, and the refusal comes from the service behind the console rather than from anything a request carries. So the ids stay in the picker and the refusal surfaces as `400 free_tier_restricted` instead of a hidden row | | Only one API shape can be served per route — the rest answer `500` once the basics work | **Per-model routing** — each model dispatched to the endpoint its own SDK names, read from the catalog | | Session IDs rejected with `400 MissingSessionID` | **Deterministic `ses_…` session hashing** and affinity across turns | | Subagents lose conversation context | **Parent session tracking** (`x-opencode-parent-session-id`, `x-parent-session-id`) | | Auto Review calls fail with `TRANSPORT: Connection error` | **Fallback session turn capture** preserving turn state across eval calls | | Quotas and balances are invisible | **Live dual-mode composer meter** showing Go quota or Zen pay-as-you-go | | Zen keys cause `403 EntitlementError` on Go usage | **Strict credential isolation** keeping Zen keys away from the Go endpoint | | Projects share a single `"global"` telemetry bucket | **Dynamic workspace attribution** resolved from the active `session.header.cwd` | | Gateway `/models` returns a truncated, unnamed list | **Catalog enrichment** (`models.opencode.ai`) with display names, context windows and prices | --- ## 🧭 Supported Models & Multi-Protocol Routing **Both endpoints, and both credential shapes.** OpenCode's catalog defines an endpoint at two levels: a **provider default** — `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1` for Zen, `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` for Go — and a per-model **inference** endpoint that overrides it when the catalog sets one (the CLI reads `model.api.url`, falling back to the provider default). The plugin pins neither: it matches the `opencode.ai/zen` marker, so a model served from the default and a model served from its own endpoint are both patched. Those endpoints authenticate in **two ways**, because they speak three wire shapes: the OpenAI planes send `Authorization: Bearer `, the Anthropic plane sends `x-api-key: `. The plugin reads **both** — `Authorization` first, then `x-api-key` / `api-key` — so a credential is captured whichever plane carried it, and the Go quota read still finds a key. The gateway serves four protocol families, and **OpenAI alone is two of them**: Chat Completions and Responses are different wire formats, not two names for one thing. A model that needs Responses does not work on the completions endpoint, and the gateway does not fall back — it answers `500`. DSH speaks three of the four families itself. The fourth — Google Generative AI — is served by **this patch's own adapter**, registered on the host's `llm` service under the route `opencode-google`, so all four are routed. See the table below. ### 1. OpenCode Zen (`provider: opencode`) — pay-as-you-go & free tier - **Anthropic Messages** (`https://opencode.ai/inference/anthropic/v1/messages`): `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-haiku-4-5`, `qwen3.8-flash` - **OpenAI Responses** (`https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1/responses`): `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.2`, `gpt-5.1-codex-max`, `muse-spark-1.3`, `grok-4.7`, `muse-wonder-1.0` - **OpenAI Chat Completions** (`https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1/chat/completions`): `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `kimi-k2.5`, `kimi-k3`, `minimax-m2.5`, `glm-5.2`, plus free-tier `mimo-v2.6-flash-free`, `nemotron-3.5-lightning-free`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` - **Google Generative AI** (`https://opencode.ai/inference/google/v1beta/models/*:streamGenerateContent`), served by this patch's adapter as `opencode-google`: `gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.1-pro`, `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` ### 2. OpenCode Go (`provider: opencode-go`) — subscription quota - **Google Generative AI** (`https://opencode.ai/inference/go/google/v1beta/models/*:streamGenerateContent`): `gemini-4-argon`, served by the internal `opencode-go-google` adapter. Add the model under your existing `opencode-go` provider; the bridge inherits that provider's API key reference (default `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY`). It supports image attachments and signed tool-call replay. Only configured models are mounted; access still depends on your Go plan. This endpoint is also used with `endpoint: legacy`, because Go has no legacy Google endpoint. - **OpenAI Chat Completions** (`https://opencode.ai/inference/go/openai/v1/chat/completions`): `beam-free`, `deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `glm-5.2`, `glm-5.3`, `glm-5.3-flash`, `hy3`, `hy4-preview`, `iceman-contributor-free`, `kimi-k2.7-code`, `kimi-k3`, `kimi-k3.1-pro`, `longcat-2.0`, `mimo-v2.5`, `mimo-v2.5-pro`, `mimo-v2.6-flash`, `mimo-v2.6-pro`, `minimax-m3.1-flash`, `step-5-preview` - **OpenAI Responses** (`https://opencode.ai/inference/go/openai/v1/responses`): `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-6-luna`, `grok-4.7`, `muse-spark-1.2-contributor`, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` - **Anthropic Messages** (`https://opencode.ai/inference/go/anthropic/v1/messages`): `claude-haiku-5-5`, `minimax-m3`, `qwen3.7-plus`, `qwen3.8-flash`, `qwen3.8-max` - Monitored by the live 3-window quota meter (5-hour rolling, weekly, monthly). The full set ships in the bundled catalog — see [Authoritative Model Catalogs](#7-authoritative-model-catalogs-dual-local-shims--real-time-swr-updates). ### 3. How a model's protocol is chosen — and why you configure nothing Zen's provider-level SDK is `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`. models.dev names a **different** SDK per model only when that model needs one, so the presence of `provider.npm` is the signal — and it is what decides the wire protocol. Nothing is matched by hand: | models.dev `provider.npm` | models | protocol | served from | | :-- | --: | :-- | :-- | | _(absent)_ | 25 | OpenAI Chat Completions | the route you configured | | `@ai-sdk/openai` | 31 | OpenAI Responses | `opencode-responses` | | `@ai-sdk/anthropic` | 17 | Anthropic Messages | `opencode-anthropic` | | `@ai-sdk/google` | 8 | Google Generative AI | `opencode-google` | | `@ai-sdk/mistral` | 1 | _(a dialect this plugin does not serve)_ | **not offered** | Counts are the **82** active `opencode` models in `models.opencode.ai` as of 2026-11-04 — everything else the vendor lists is deprecated or retired, and the patch ships only what the gateway still serves. The same 82 are bundled offline in `src/catalog-data.ts`, so every one of them routes correctly before the first catalog refresh; regenerate that file with `pnpm run catalog:shim -- --write` (without `--write` it only checks). The patch **keeps those two routes out of both the model picker and _Settings → Models_**. Three properties hold today, and one does not yet: - **You keep choosing.** The picker shows exactly the models you listed, and each one is matched to the right protocol automatically. The paid models work with a key; see [docs/opencode-1.19-api.md](./docs/opencode-1.19-api.md) for what was excluded and how | | `400 MissingSessionID` | No session header attached | Ensure `dsh-opencode-patch` is listed in the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` | | Auto Review fails with `TRANSPORT: Connection error` | Host process not restarted since the update | Stop and restart `dsh web` so the new `lib/index.mjs` loads | | Quota ring never appears for a Go model | **Restart `dsh web`, then read the browser console** — the plugin is loaded through a `link:`, so `lib/index.mjs` is read once at process start and a page reload alone keeps the old host code; the meter reports which of its paths returned nothing | The console names the cause: `no remote to mount on`, `did not mount` with the exception, `still waiting for remote.opencodeGoUsage`, `no opencodeGoUsage service on the remote` with the keys it does expose, or `the answer is not a usage shape` with what came back. A missing or unroutable credential is one cause of several, not the only one | | A catalog model is missing from Settings → Fetch, or a retired one persists | Stale host module, enrichment off, or the adapter answered from its packaged catalog | `pnpm run build`, restart `dsh web`, keep **Enrich model metadata** on, fetch from the matching route, search the exact id (e.g. `space-bunny-free`) | | Popover shows “Limit reached” in red | 100% of a rolling/monthly window reached | Open the [OpenCode Console](https://opencode.ai/console) and enable _Use balance_ to overflow into Zen credits | | Non-OpenCode models misbehaving | Unrelated to this patch | Traffic to other providers passes through untouched | --- ## Changed in 1.x - **A smaller public API.** The package's entry exports `apply`, `Config`, `inject` and `name` — the names the host reads — and the config types (`PluginConfig`, `ResolvedPluginConfig`, `ModelOverrideConfig`, `ModelRouteConfig`, `EndpointFamily`, `KeySourcePolicy`). Everything else it used to re-export is internal now. - **`./src/*` is no longer an export.** `src/` was never in the published files, so the subpath resolved in the repository and nowhere else. - **`internalRoutes` was removed.** The per-protocol routes always mount. A profile row that still carries `internalRoutes` validates and the key is ignored. - **`@viztor/dsh-opencode` is deprecated, and still published.** It is a thin wrapper that re-exports `dsh-opencode-patch`, so an install on the old name keeps resolving; the registry marks it deprecated and points at the canonical name. New installs should use `dsh-opencode-patch` or `@viztor/dsh-opencode-patch`. ## 📜 Compatibility & Verification **Verified on DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1` — both the `alpha` and `rc` channels (Node 24+)** The harness publishes two **channels**, `alpha` and `rc`, and they are parallel tracks rather than a version ordering: semver sorts `0.2.1-rc.2` _above_ `0.2.1-alpha.5`. The plugin targets two lines on both channels: **`0.2.1`**, whose `rc` builds `dsh@latest` still carries, and the **`0.2.2`** prereleases on both channels: `alpha` is at `0.2.2-alpha.3`, and `rc` opened the line with `0.2.2-rc.1` (published under the `next` dist-tag; the test install runs `0.2.2-alpha.2`). The `@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol` peer range says so exactly: ``` >=0.2.1-alpha.1 <0.3.0 || >=0.2.2-0 <0.3.0 ``` The first clause covers the `0.2.1` line on both channels: its lower bound (`alpha.1`) sorts below every `rc` of the same line, so rc needs no separate entry. The second is **not** redundant — semver excludes prereleases unless a comparator in the same `major.minor.patch` tuple carries one, so `<0.3.0` alone would silently drop every `0.2.2-*` build, alpha and rc alike. Both clauses stop at `0.3.0`, which leaves the next line a separate decision rather than a silent widening. The optional `@deepseek-ai/cordis` peer follows the typert range. Each line moved the host core: the `0.2.1` builds peer `~4.0.5` (or a `4.0.5` prerelease), the `0.2.2` alphas a `4.0.6` prerelease, and `0.2.2-rc.1` `~4.1.0`. A fresh install takes the cordis the **newest** admitted typert build peers on, so a cordis peer that misses it fails with `ERESOLVE`; one that misses an older line's cordis fails beside a host already installed on that line. --- `dsh-opencode-patch` 是一个 DeepSeek Harness 宿主插件，让 **OpenCode Zen 与 Go** 模型在 DSH 内持续可用。无需遭遇网络拒绝、Cloudflare 挑战、权益不匹配或隐形限制，即可接入 `claude-sonnet-4-5`、`gpt-5.4`、`gemini-3.8-flash`、`deepseek-v4.1-flash`、`muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free`、`qwen3.8-flash` 以及 OpenCode 目录中的其余模型。 **默认状态。** 把 DSH 直接指向 OpenCode、不装任何插件，模型是**完全不能用**的——不是某一种形状不能用，而是全部： - **请求不会被识别为"编码 agent"发出的。** DSH 发的是自己的 `User-Agent`，不带 `x-opencode-client`、`x-opencode-project`，也不带 `x-opencode-session`；网关看到的就是一次匿名 SDK 调用，流量要受厂商对"不表明身份的客户端"所设的滥用规则约束。**免费层是另一回事，原因也不在这里**：把这些请求头全部恢复、换上 CLI 的 `User-Agent`、带上有效的会话 id 以及回退注入的 `read`/`bash` 工具定义之后，在 OpenCode 之外调用 Zen 的 `-free` 模型仍然返回 `403 FreeTierError`，而同一个请求换成付费模型返回 `200`。这些 id 依然会列出——拒绝本身会说明原因，而把厂商可能仍在服务的模型藏起来是更糟的失败——补丁恢复的请求头服务于付费路由以及厂商声明的客户端规则。 - **没有会话 id 的一轮会被拒、或失去关联。** 每一轮都必须带一个稳定的 `ses_…` 形状的 id，而 DSH 在子代理、后台评估以及 **Auto Review** 这类模式下会完全省略 `sessionId`。 - **免费层的 `/responses` 请求体缺少 `read` 与 `bash` 会被拒**，而 DSH 是刻意不发这两个工具的。 - **目录很单薄。** 裸 `/models` 列表只有 id，几乎没有别的信息，所以选择器里是一堆没有名字、没有价格、没有上下文窗口的行。 **这些能用之后剩下的**是另一个问题，而且与账号无关：OpenCode 的模型分布在**四种不同的 API 形状**上，而 DSH 是按 provider 行选择传输协议的——一条路由只能说一种形状。所以走 Responses / Messages / Mistral 的模型在基础问题解决之后就会返回 `500`。这正是插件**按模型而不是按 provider** 路由的原因。 插件在网络层补齐所有缺失的协议要素——**且仅针对 OpenCode 路由**（`opencode` / `opencode-go` / `opencode-responses` / `opencode-anthropic` / `opencode-google`）。其余全部流量（DeepSeek、OpenAI、Anthropic、GitHub）原样通过。 **三条主线。** 1. **最小侵入。** 不做全局补丁：只拦截本插件声明的路由，其他厂商——DeepSeek、OpenAI、Anthropic、GitHub——的请求原样通过。计量器离"彻底消失"只差一个开关，而不是离"勉强忍受"隔着一个页面。 2. **原生 DSH 插件。** 一个 `apply()`、一张绑定自己命名空间的设置卡、用 `ctx.inject` 声明服务、按宿主自己的方式填充插槽，文案随宿主语言切换。没有私有钩子，不改宿主代码。 3. **OpenCode API 兼容。** 网关真正检查的那些特征在网络层还原——与 CLI 同形状的 `ses_…` 会话 id、官方来源头、父会话血统，以及免费层的 `read`/`bash` 工具 schema 回退。 **亮点** - # Contributing to dsh-opencode-patch

## Prerequisites

- Node.js `>= 24` (CI runs the version in `.node-version`, and the floor in a job of its own), `pnpm` (v12). The suite refuses to start below the floor and names both versions: below it, `node:sqlite`, `Intl.DurationFormat` and the ICU strings the tests pin differ, and the failures read like regressions.
- A checkout of this repo; for live testing, a DeepSeek Harness profile (see README for the `link:` setup)

## Commands

All tasks go through `pnpm` (which delegates to the Vite+ toolchain):

```sh
pnpm install     # install dependencies
pnpm run check   # format + lint + types; must be zero *errors* (warnings are reported, not gating)
pnpm run test    # Vitest suite, must be fully green and deterministic
pnpm run test:coverage   # the same run, with the coverage ratchet enforced
pnpm run test:shuffle    # the same run in a random order; reproduce a failure with --sequence.seed=<n>
pnpm run test:mock       # gateway mock suite: offline, loopback only, runs in CI
pnpm run build   # vp pack + client rename -> lib/index.mjs, lib/index.d.mts, lib/client.js
pnpm run test:e2e   # opt-in end-to-end suite; talks to the real OpenCode gateway
pnpm run catalog:shim   # is src/catalog-data.ts current? (-- --write regenerates it from models.dev)
pnpm run limits:shim    # is src/go-limits-data.ts current? (-- --write regenerates it)
pnpm run cli:version    # is the pinned OpenCode CLI version the published one?
```

> Note: in some shells `pnpm exec` stalls; invoke the binary directly if so: `node node_modules/.pnpm/vite-plus@*/node_modules/vite-plus/bin/vp <cmd>`.

## End-to-end suite

`pnpm run test:e2e` runs `test/e2e/**/*.e2e.ts` through its own config (`vitest.e2e.config.ts`), so `pnpm run test` stays a fully offline, deterministic unit run. Nothing here is collected by the unit suite.

```sh
OPENCODE_E2E=1 OPENCODE_API_KEY=… OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY=… pnpm run test:e2e
```

- `OPENCODE_E2E=1` is required; without it every case skips, so a bare `pnpm run test:e2e` is a safe no-op.
- `OPENCODE_API_KEY` (Zen) arms the live `/models` enrichment case and the **paid** protocol-routing cases; `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` (Go plan) arms the live `/usage` case. Each block skips when its key is absent, which is why the CI `e2e` job stays green on fork PRs (secrets are not exposed to them) while still checking the endpoints answer.
- The **free-tier and unmetered** routing cases run keyless on purpose: measured 2026-10-06, a paid model answers `401 AuthError` on every endpoint without a credential, so keyless probing cannot tell them apart at all. Keyless discrimination is real only for the free classes.
- `OPENCODE_ZEN_BASE_URL` / `OPENCODE_GO_BASE_URL` retarget the suite at a mirror.

The e2e files, one job each:

- `opencode-live.e2e.ts` — the only place the plugin meets the real API. It catches what a stub cannot: **the vendor changing the payload**. The meter parses `/zen/go/v1/usage` and the picker consumes an enriched `/models` listing, so both shapes are asserted against the live service. The unkeyed cases assert reachability (never a 404) and that our header set does not change the gateway's verdict on a request — compared against the same call without it, rather than hardcoding a status the vendor may tighten.
- `patched-fetch-headers.e2e.ts` — a local `node:http` listener, so the _outgoing_ header set crosses a real socket. The live gateway cannot echo a request back; everywhere else in the suite the injected headers are asserted against a captured `fetch`.
- `protocol-routing.e2e.ts` — one turn per protocol against the live gateway: the vendor-side claim that a model's `provider_npm` names its wire format, which a unit test can only read back from our own table.
- `refusal-classification.e2e.ts` — the host's error classifier fed the gateway's measured refusals over a real `node:http` socket, chunked bodies included, after asserting the installed bundle still carries the branches the verdicts rely on.
- `dispatch-levels.e2e.ts` — no network: the installed pi's own level rule against both decorators across the shipped catalog, so every reasoning level the picker offers is one dispatch accepts.

## Live profile loop

The web profile wires this checkout with `link:`, so builds are picked up like this:

- **Host (`lib/index.mjs`) — restart required.** The base bundle ships `hmr root: []` (config watches only, `**/node_modules` ignored) and the loader caches ESM imports per process, so a linked package is never re-imported after boot. After every `pnpm run build`, restart `dsh web` — otherwise the profile silently keeps running the module from boot time. Symptom of a stale host: the plugin row is active but the settings card shows "This plugin is not loaded, so it cannot be configured." — `dsh-settings` is filtering on the old module's `Config` schema.
- **Client (`lib/client.js`) — refresh suffices.** The client bundle is re-served from disk on every page load; a browser refresh picks it up.
- **Verify after a restart:** the Plugins page shows the **OpenCode Patch** card, and its configure view renders every card field (`CARD_FIELDS` in `src/settings-fields.ts`; the `CONFIG_ONLY_FIELDS` knobs stay off the card by design) and no unavailable line. `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/check.ts` catches a stale `lib/` before you do (`src/` newer than `lib/`).

## Code conventions

- **100% strict TypeScript.** No `any` leaks, no `as` assertions in `src/` — narrow `unknown` with `in`-operator type guards (`isRecord`, `isUnknownArray`, …).
- **Zero errors; warnings are reported, not gating** (the `pnpm run check` line above). `release:gate` and CI fail on an error; warnings become gating in phase P12 of `docs/improvement-plan.md`, so do not add one. The `error` tier is reserved for defects: async safety and throw contracts. If a rule fights a correct pattern (e.g. sync Promise wrappers that preserve `AsyncLocalStorage` context), prefer a targeted `oxlint-disable` comment with justification over weakening the rule globally.
- **Sync-over-async for context propagation.** `withStore` iterators and the `fetch` patch intentionally return promises from non-`async` functions so `als.run()` keeps turn context without an extra tick. Don't "fix" these into `async`.
- **Style:** arrow-function consts (not `function` declarations), dot notation, explicit `=== undefined` checks, `oxfmt` formatting.

## Test conventions

- **Deterministic only.** No `Math.random()`, no fixed `sleep()` waits. Async file assertions poll with a deadline (`waitForFileContent`).
- **No secret fixtures.** Session IDs are derived at runtime (`openCodeSessionIdFor`) or read from `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`; never hardcode `ses_…` or API keys. `lib/` and `*.log` stay gitignored.
- **Restore globals.** Tests that touch `globalThis.fetch` or `process.env` must restore them in `afterEach` (`vi.unstubAllGlobals()`, `delete process.env.…`).
- **Offline by construction.** `test/support/offline.ts` refuses every non-loopback request in the unit and mock suites. The catalog's background revalidation used to reach `models.opencode.ai` dozens of times per run, so a networked runner's results could depend on the vendor's live catalog. A case that means to fetch stubs `fetch` itself.
- **No order dependence.** `test/support/reset-process-state.ts` clears the plugin's module-level stores (captured keys, session spend, the live catalog) after every test. A new module-level store gets a reset next to its siblings. `pnpm run test:shuffle` is how to check, and CI runs it.
- **Tests reach `src` through `test/support/src.ts`.** It re-exports, from each defining module, everything a test needs, so a module move or a barrel change edits one file instead of thirty. A new test imports from `./support/src.ts` (`../support/src.ts` under `test/mock` and `test/e2e`); add a missing name there rather than importing a `src` path. The exceptions are `vi.mock("../src/x.ts")` targets (and their `importOriginal<typeof import(…)>` type), which must name the module; fresh-module re-imports after `vi.resetModules()`, whose subject is module identity; the architecture and public-API tests, whose subject is the `src` layout and the barrel; the jsdom (client) tests, which import the defining module directly, because `src.ts` re-exports the host graph (`node:sqlite`, pi, `lifecycle.ts`) and the next rule keeps that out of client tests; and the setup file `test/support/reset-process-state.ts`, which runs before the jsdom tests too. `test/architecture.test.ts` fails on a static or side-effect `src` import anywhere else, on a dynamic `import("../src/…")` in a file that never calls `vi.resetModules()`, and on a jsdom test that value-imports the door. Importing the door loads the whole `src` graph, host and client, so a module that fails to load fails every test that comes through it.
- **Host-only fixtures stay out of shared helpers.** `test/test-helpers.ts` is imported by the jsdom (client) tests, so anything that needs `node:sqlite` or the filesystem belongs in `test/support/`, as `opencode-store-fixture.ts` does.
- **A test for a fix fails without it.** Before committing a regression test, revert the fix locally and watch it fail.
- **Meaningful coverage.** Every config field in the `SPECS` register (`src/settings-fields.ts`) needs both the on and off path where it has one; every passthrough claim needs a non-OpenCode URL test proving headers are untouched; helper functions exported from `usage-ui.ts` are asserted directly, not re-derived in the test.
- **A component with hooks needs a real mount.** Calling `Component(props)` returns an element and runs none of its state, so a hook-bearing component can have twenty passing cases and still be untested — `usage-pill.tsx` sat at 9% exactly that way, with the poll loop, retry and dismissal all uncovered. `test/usage-pill-mount.test.tsx` is the answer: a `// @vitest-environment jsdom` pragma scoped to that one file, so the rest of the suite keeps the fast node environment and the zero-dependency element-tree style.

### The coverage ratchet

`pnpm run test:coverage` runs the same suite with thresholds from `vite.config.ts`. They are a **ratchet, not a target**: they sit at the level the suite actually reaches, so they fail when coverage DROPS and nothing else. Two rules follow.

- **Raise them when you genuinely add coverage** — a PR that lifts statements by a few points should lift the threshold with it, or the next contributor inherits a gate nobody re-measured.
- **Never set one above the current measurement.** That does not make the suite better; it makes every subsequent PR fail until someone deletes tests.

`src/index.ts` is excluded from the report — it is a pure re-export barrel, and the coverage tools attribute an untaken re-export line to whichever file re-exports it, so leaving it in reports a hole nobody can fill while hiding real ones. `responses-provider.ts` and `responses-routes.ts` carry their own per-file floors: the mount has four host contracts to survive, and a well-covered average must not be able to hide it.

## The freshness checks in CI

The `catalog freshness` job runs three checks against what the vendor publishes: `catalog:shim` (the bundled catalog, `src/catalog-data.ts`), `limits:shim` (the Go allowances, `src/go-limits-data.ts`) and `cli:version` (the pinned CLI version in `src/identity.ts`). The vendor moves all three most days, so what a run does with a mismatch depends on whether the change under test could have caused it.

- **A pull request is gated on a check only when its own diff touches that check's inputs.** The inputs are the check's script and every local module it loads, transitively, plus `src/identity.ts` for `cli:version`, which the script reads as data. The edges are the ones Node loads: the source's types are erased by Node's own stripper and the specifiers read by a real lexer, so a whole-statement `import type` loads nothing and is no edge, and an import written in a string or template is not one either; anything else is, so the set reaches further than the generator's own folder: the catalog parser loads `src/config.ts`, so a settings change gates `catalog:shim`. `scripts/freshness-scope.ts` derives the inputs from the sources and answers `gate` or `report` for the diff (`git diff --name-only HEAD^1 HEAD` on the merge ref). Change `src/models-catalog.ts` and forget to regenerate, and the pull request fails; that omission is what the gate exists to catch.
- **One half of `cli:version` gates every pull request.** The script checks two things: that every copy of the CLI version in `src/`, `test/`, `docs/`, `scripts/` and `README.md` agrees with `src/identity.ts`, and that the pin is the published version. The first is offline and skips the two generated tables (they hold the vendor's data, not copies the repository maintains), so only the repository can break it, and `pnpm run cli:version -- --copies` runs on every pull request as a gate. Only the registry comparison is scoped as above, and when it only warns, the warning quotes the script's own `error:` line.
- **Otherwise the check reports.** A stale file is a `::warning::`, the job stays green, and the nightly run regenerates both files and opens the refresh as a pull request of its own. A stale CLI pin is only warned about, by every run including the nightly; bumping it is a human pull request to `src/identity.ts` and its copies, which is then gated, because the pin is an input. Vendor drift is not a regression your pull request introduced, so it is not a reason to fail it.
- **The generated files are never inputs.** A pull request that carries only a refresh reports. One that changes `src/catalog-data.ts` or `src/go-limits-data.ts` without touching what generates it gets a warning naming the file, because those files are never edited by hand.
- **A push to `main` reports.** The nightly run regenerates the two generated files and opens the refresh as a pull request; for the CLI version it warns. A manual dispatch only reports the CLI version. None of these paths gates, for the same reason.
- **The gates fail closed.** Each runs unless the scope step answered `report`, so a lost answer gates every pull request rather than skipping the check.

To see the answer for your branch before CI does:

```sh
git diff --name-only main... \
  | node --experimental-strip-types --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning scripts/freshness-scope.ts catalog:shim
```

## Release process (maintainers)

1. Use conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`) — release-please opens the version-bump + changelog PR automatically; merging it tags and creates the GitHub Release, which fires OIDC publishing to npm and GitHub Packages.
2. Avoid manual releases: release-please anchors on the latest GitHub **Release**, not the latest tag, so a bare tag is invisible to it (`AGENTS.md`, "Releasing"). If one is unavoidable, bump `version` in `package.json`, commit, tag, push the tag, and create the GitHub Release in the same step (`gh release create vX.Y.Z --generate-notes`). Never touch `CHANGELOG.md`: release-please owns it.
3. On every release, refresh the **Verified on DeepSeek Harness** line and its matrix under "Compatibility & Verification" in both READMEs after smoke-testing: registry install resolves, plugin loads in the DSH Web profile, and a free-tier Zen call succeeds.

## Docs

- `README.md` is consumer-facing: problem-first, install, UI config, troubleshooting. No dev internals.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is the per-version record. `AGENTS.md` is the agent-facing project brief — keep it specific to this repo.
